model.name: EU AI Act with ISO/IEC 42001 (starter)
model.documentation: An AI system inventory classified by the risk tiers of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the provider and deployer obligations that follow, article by article, and the ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management system clauses and Annex A control areas that meet them. Each AI system records its risk classification, the organisation's role towards it (provider, deployer or both) and the legal basis for the classification. Article summaries are paraphrased and ISO/IEC 42001 is cited by clause and control area title only. Replace the example lender's AI systems with your own inventory. This model is a structuring aid, not legal advice.

element.name: EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
element.documentation: In force since 1 August 2024 and amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Prohibitions have applied since 2 February 2025 and general-purpose AI model obligations since 2 August 2025. High-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and from 2 August 2028 for systems covered by Annex I.

element.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management systems
element.documentation: The international standard for an AI management system. Certification is against clauses 4 to 10, with Annex A as the reference set of controls.

element.name: Lawful, trustworthy use of AI
element.documentation: Every AI system the organisation builds or uses is known, classified, and governed in line with its risk.

element.name: Provider obligations for high-risk AI systems
element.documentation: Chapter III, Sections 2 and 3: requirements for the system and duties of its provider.

element.name: Deployer obligations for high-risk AI systems
element.documentation: Duties of the organisation using a high-risk system under its authority.

element.name: Obligations for every AI system
element.documentation: Prohibited practices and transparency duties, whatever the risk tier.

element.name: Article 5: Prohibited AI practices
element.documentation: AI practices that may not be placed on the market or used at all, among them emotion recognition in the workplace or in education except for medical or safety reasons.

element.name: Article 9: Risk management system
element.documentation: A risk management process run across the whole life cycle of a high-risk system: identify and evaluate risks, adopt measures, and test against them.

element.name: Article 10: Data and data governance
element.documentation: Training, validation and testing data governed for relevance, representativeness, errors, completeness and possible bias.

element.name: Article 11: Technical documentation
element.documentation: Technical documentation drawn up before the system is placed on the market and kept up to date, covering the elements set out in Annex IV.

element.name: Article 12: Record-keeping
element.documentation: Automatic logging of events over the system's lifetime, so its operation can be traced.

element.name: Article 13: Transparency and information to deployers
element.documentation: Instructions for use that let deployers understand the system's output, capabilities, limitations and oversight measures.

element.name: Article 14: Human oversight
element.documentation: Design that lets natural persons oversee the system effectively, understand its limits, override its output and stop it.

element.name: Article 15: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
element.documentation: Appropriate, declared levels of accuracy, resilience to errors and inconsistencies, and protection against attempts to alter use or performance.

element.name: Article 17: Quality management system
element.documentation: Documented policies, procedures and accountability that assure compliance across design, development, testing, data management and monitoring.

element.name: Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
element.documentation: Use the system as instructed, assign competent human oversight, keep input data relevant, monitor operation and report risks and serious incidents, keep logs for at least six months, inform workers' representatives before workplace use, and tell people when a high-risk system helps make decisions about them.

element.name: Article 27: Fundamental rights impact assessment
element.documentation: Before first use, public bodies, private entities providing public services, and deployers of credit scoring or life and health insurance pricing systems assess the processes, affected groups, risks of harm, oversight and remedies.

element.name: Article 50: Transparency for certain AI systems
element.documentation: People are told when they interact with an AI system; generated content is marked as such in a machine-readable way; deep fakes and emotion recognition are disclosed.

element.name: Article 72: Post-market monitoring
element.documentation: A post-market monitoring system and plan that collects and analyses performance data throughout the system's lifetime.

element.name: Article 73: Reporting of serious incidents
element.documentation: Serious incidents reported to the market surveillance authority immediately and at the latest within 15 days of awareness; 2 days for a widespread infringement or serious disruption of critical infrastructure; 10 days where a person has died.

element.name: Article 53: Obligations of general-purpose AI model providers
element.documentation: Technical documentation, information for downstream providers, a copyright policy and a public summary of training content.

element.name: Prohibited
element.documentation: Article 5. May not be placed on the market, put into service or used.

element.name: High-risk
element.documentation: Article 6 with Annexes I and III. Subject to Chapter III requirements before and after being placed on the market.

element.name: Limited risk
element.documentation: Article 50 transparency obligations.

element.name: Minimal risk
element.documentation: No specific obligations under the Act.

element.name: General-purpose AI model
element.documentation: Chapter V. Obligations on the model provider, with more for models with systemic risk.

element.name: Staff emotion monitoring
element.documentation: Proposal to read staff emotions on video calls. Rejected at intake and never deployed.

property.value: Article 5: emotion recognition in the workplace

element.name: CV screening assistant
element.documentation: Ranks job applications for recruiters. Bought from a vendor, who is the provider.

property.value: Annex III point 4: recruitment and selection

element.name: Credit scoring model
element.documentation: Scores consumer loan applications. Built in-house and used by the lending team.

property.value: Annex III point 5(b): creditworthiness of natural persons

element.name: Customer service chatbot
element.documentation: Answers customer questions on the website, built on a third-party general-purpose model.

element.name: Email spam and phishing filter
element.documentation: Filters inbound email. Voluntary codes of conduct apply.

element.name: General-purpose language model
element.documentation: Third-party model accessed through an API. Powers the customer service chatbot.

property.value: Chapter V: obligations rest on the model provider

element.name: Model provider
element.documentation: Provider of the general-purpose model, bound by Article 53.

element.name: ISO/IEC 42001 requirements (clauses 4 to 10)
element.documentation: The requirements a certified AI management system must meet.

element.name: Clause 4: Context of the organisation
element.documentation: Internal and external issues, interested parties, the organisation's roles towards AI systems, and the scope of the AI management system.

element.name: AI management system scope and inventory
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process that meets this clause in your organisation.

element.name: Clause 5: Leadership
element.documentation: Top management commitment, an AI policy, and assigned roles, responsibilities and authorities.

element.name: AI policy approval and role assignment
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process that meets this clause in your organisation.

element.name: Clause 6: Planning
element.documentation: AI risk assessment and treatment, AI system impact assessment, a statement of applicability for the Annex A controls, and AI objectives.

element.name: AI risk assessment and treatment
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process that meets this clause in your organisation.

element.name: Clause 7: Support
element.documentation: Resources, competence, awareness, communication and documented information.

element.name: AI competence and awareness programme
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process that meets this clause in your organisation.

element.name: Clause 8: Operation
element.documentation: Operational planning and control, with risk assessments, risk treatment and impact assessments carried out when planned and when things change.

element.name: AI use case intake and classification
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process that meets this clause in your organisation.

element.name: Clause 9: Performance evaluation
element.documentation: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation, internal audit and management review.

element.name: AI internal audit and management review
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process that meets this clause in your organisation.

element.name: Clause 10: Improvement
element.documentation: Continual improvement, nonconformity and corrective action.

element.name: AI corrective action
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process that meets this clause in your organisation.

element.name: Statement of applicability
element.documentation: Lists each Annex A control, whether it applies, why, and whether it is implemented.

element.name: ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A control areas
element.documentation: Nine control objective areas, A.2 to A.10.

element.name: A.2 Policies related to AI
element.documentation: An AI policy aligned with other organisational policies and reviewed. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.3 Internal organisation
element.documentation: Defined AI roles and responsibilities and a way to report concerns. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.4 Resources for AI systems
element.documentation: Data, tooling, computing and human resources documented for each AI system. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.5 Assessing impacts of AI systems
element.documentation: A process to assess and document impacts of AI systems on individuals, groups and society. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.6 AI system life cycle
element.documentation: Responsible design, development, verification, deployment, operation, monitoring and event logging of AI systems. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.7 Data for AI systems
element.documentation: Data acquisition, quality, provenance and preparation managed for AI systems. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.8 Information for interested parties
element.documentation: Documentation and information for users, reporting of adverse impacts and communication of incidents. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.9 Use of AI systems
element.documentation: Processes and objectives for responsible use of AI systems within their intended use. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

element.name: A.10 Third-party and customer relationships
element.documentation: Responsibilities shared with suppliers, partners and customers, and supplier management. Example control area; record the controls you apply in the statement of applicability.

view.name: AI system inventory and risk classification
view.documentation: Every AI system in the organisation, sorted into the Act's risk tiers, with the obligations each one brings. Record the organisation's role for each system: a deployer that substantially modifies a high-risk system, or puts its own name on it, becomes its provider.

view.name: AI Act obligations and ISO 42001 controls
view.documentation: Each obligation of the Act beside the ISO/IEC 42001 control area or process that meets it, grouped so each control's obligations sit together. An article with nothing drawn to it is a gap in the management system.

view.name: ISO 42001 AI management system
view.documentation: Clauses 4 to 10 of ISO/IEC 42001, each with the process that meets it, and the statement of applicability that selects the Annex A controls.
